title: Private Deployments: VPC & On‑Prem Comprehensive Deployment, Day‑2 Ops, Upgrade and Rollback
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This document is a single authoritative reference for private deployments of Redwood Inference in VPC and on‑prem environments. It consolidates recommended reference architectures, packaging guidance, operational runbooks for day‑2 activities, and validated upgrade & rollback procedures. The intended audience is platform engineers, SREs, and solutions engineers responsible for deploying and operating Redwood Private at customer sites.

Scope
- Target platforms: AWS VPC (Private deployment mode), Azure VNet, GCP VPC, and air‑gapped on‑prem clusters (OpenShift/Kubernetes or bare metal orchestrated).
- Components covered: control plane (customer‑managed control plane for Private), inference runtime, storage (model/artifact stores), networking and ingress, KMS/HSM integrations, observability (metrics/tracing/logs), and day‑2 operational procedures.
- Not covered: product roadmap, hosting of Redwood hosted API, or developer onboarding for hosted tenants.

Key goals
- Repeatable, secure deployment patterns for customers with regulatory requirements.
- Deterministic upgrade path with safety checks and rollback built into the process.
- Clear day‑2 operations and runbooks for common incidents and maintenance tasks.

Owners & SLAs
- Document owner: eng-private-deployments (team).
- Primary contact: Asha Patel (Private Deployments PM).
- Operational owners: SRE oncall rotation + Private Deployments Solutions Engineering.
- Target SLOs for Private deployments (customer contract dependent):
  - Control plane: 99.9% availability (monthly).
  - Inference latency tail (p95): per customer SLA (baseline 150ms for <2048 tokens on Dedicated GPU pools).
  - Model load success rate: 99.95% per deployment.

Reference architectures (patterns)
1) Small footprint (Proof-of-Concept / PoC)
- 1 control plane node (HA not required for PoC).
- 1 worker (GPU host) with single model slot.
- Use cloud-managed DB for state (RDS/Azure SQL) and S3-compatible object store.
- TLS for all ingress; KMS integration optional.

2) Production VPC (recommended)
- Control plane: 3 replicas (stateless API / stateful control components separated), Frontend load balancer in private subnets.
- Inference pool: Autoscaling GPU node pool behind internal load balancer with nodegroup spread across AZs.
- Storage: S3 (or S3 compatible) in same region, encrypted at rest (KMS).
- Network: Private subnets for services, NAT for outbound control plane updates, VPC endpoints for S3 and KMS.
- Observability stack: Prometheus/Thanos (metrics), Loki (logs), Jaeger/OTel (traces).
- Access controls: RBAC via the customer IdP + mTLS between components.

3) Air‑gapped on‑prem (regulated/isolated)
- Full customer-managed control plane inside an isolated network.
- On‑prem model artifact registry (minIO or equivalent) with signed manifest verification.
- Image distribution via secure air‑gap transfer procedures (signed tarballs + manifest).
- HSM/KMS via network‑segregated appliance or local HSM with plugin.

Networking & security checklist (table)
- Required: Private subnets for control plane and inference, internal ALBs, VPC endpoints, KMS integration, Private DNS.
- Recommended: Service‑mesh (mTLS), network policies, egress whitelisting, scan for open ports.

Deployment prerequisites (customer checklist)
1) Identity & Access
- Customer IdP details for SSO.
- Service account with least privilege for cloud resources.

2) Network
- CIDR allocations for private subnets, route tables, and NAT requirements.
- Public IP plan for bastion/jump hosts if required.

3) Storage & Secrets
- S3 bucket (or equivalent) with versioning + lifecycle rules.
- KMS key ARN and access policy.

4) Compute
- GPU instance type list and quotas approved (e.g., A100 / H100 families), node sizing guidance based on expected QPS.

Packaging and on‑prem artifacts
- Distribution formats supported: OCI images (preferred), tarball bundles for air‑gap.
- Package layout for tarball: 
  - release-manifest.yaml (signed by Redwood release key)
  - images/ (OCI image tar files)
  - artifacts/models/ (optional initial model bundle)
  - checksums.sha256

Sample release-manifest.yaml snippet:

apiVersion: redwood/v1
release: "2027.03.01"
components:
  - name: control-plane
    version: "1.6.2"
    digest: "sha256:..."

Verification steps after unpack (air‑gap)
1. Verify signature of release-manifest.yaml using Redwood public key.
2. Validate checksums.sha256.
3. Load images into local registry with signed provenance.

VPC Deployment guide (high level steps)
1) Prepare cloud environment (IAM, VPC, subnets, routing).
2) Provision storage and KMS resources.
3) Bootstrap control plane (Helm chart / operator):
   - helm install redwood-control-plane --namespace redwood -f values-prod.yaml redwood/control-plane
4) Provision inference pools and node pools with GPU labels.
5) Configure internal ALB and Service discovery.
6) Deploy observability and alerting.
7) Smoke tests: model load, sample inference, latency checks.

Values file highlights (values-prod.yaml)
- controlPlane.replicas: 3
- storage.provider: s3
- storage.bucket: "redwood-private-<customer>-models"
- kms.keyArn: "arn:aws:kms:..."
- autoscaler.minReplicas: 2
- autoscaler.maxReplicas: 50

Day‑2 Operations (runbook highlights)
- Common maintenance tasks:
  - Add capacity: scale node pool + annotate new nodes for GPU labeling.
  - Rotate KMS keys: follow KMS rotation guide and verify model re‑encryption where required.
  - Rotate TLS certificates: update CertManager CR and perform rolling restart.

Incident triage checklist (example for inference latency spike)
1) Verify whether spike is global or zone specific (Metrics dashboard).
2) Check node-level resource pressure (GPU utilization, memory).
3) Check autoscaler activity and pending pods.
4) Confirm model caching/eviction logs.
5) If degraded due to model load failures, trigger model rollback to previous version.
6) Engage oncall and notify stakeholders per escalation policy.

Operational playbook: model rollout (canary -> scale -> promote)
1) Upload new model to staging bucket and register version.
2) Canary deployment to 5% of traffic (routing policy).
3) Monitor quality/regression signals for 24‑72 hours (evals + customer test set).
4) If OK, promote to 30% then 100% with staged autoscaling.
5) If regression detected, trigger automated fallback to previous model and create regression ticket.

Upgrade and rollback procedures
- Principles:
  - Always perform control plane upgrade in a non‑peak window.
  - Keep database and schema migrations reversible.
  - Snapshot configuration and create restore points for model stores where possible.

Control plane upgrade (high level)
1) Create a release plan with explicit versions and rollback commit IDs.
2) Notify customers and stakeholders (maintenance window).
3) Run preflight checks (cluster health, DB replication lag < 5s, storage available).
4) Perform rolling upgrade: upgrade one replica at a time and verify health checks before proceeding.
5) Run post‑upgrade integration tests (model load, inference, admin APIs).
6) If failure: initiate rollback to prior chart + image tag, monitor system for stabilization.

Inference runtime upgrade (safe pattern)
1) Canary run on segmented worker pool.
2) Run perf and correctness suite (automated benchmarks + sample prompts).
3) If anomaly, cordon and drain canary nodes, redeploy previous runtime, and tag incident for follow up.

Rollback checklist (emergency)
- Command sequence (Kubernetes example):
  - kubectl -n redwood rollout undo deployment/control-plane --to-revision=<previous-revision>
  - kubectl -n redwood set image deployment/inference-runtime inference-runtime=redwood/runtime:<previous-tag>
- Verify dependent services and rehydrate caches if necessary.

Post‑mortem and regression triage
- For any failed upgrade or significant incident, create an incident ticket and run a postmortem within 3 business days.
- Include: timeline, root cause, remediation, test gaps, and action items assigned.

Customer requirements library (summary table)
- Network: private endpoints, list of allowed egress FQDNs, CIDR ranges.
- Compliance: required audit logs retention (e.g., 365 days), SOC2/ISO evidence checklist.
- Data residency: region restrictions for model artifacts and telemetry.
- Key management: HSM or KMS integration details and rotation policy.
- Support model: contact matrix, escalation paths, and on‑site requirements.

Sample customer requirement entry (short form)
- Requirement ID: CRL-2026-001
- Title: Data residency in EU
- Description: All model artifacts and telemetry must reside in EU region and cannot be replicated to non‑EU regions.
- Acceptance criteria: S3 bucket in eu‑west‑1 only; no cross‑region replication.

Operational checklists (quick references)
- Pre‑upgrade checklist:
  - Backups taken and verified
  - Change approvals recorded
  - Monitoring alerts suppressed for minor expected changes
- Post‑upgrade checklist:
  - End‑to‑end smoke tests passed
  - Customer validation (if requested)
  - Metrics baseline comparison run (p50/p95/p99 token latency, model load time)

Appendices
- Useful CLI snippets:
  - Image import (air‑gap): skopeo copy --dest-tls-verify=false docker-archive:images.tar docker://localhost:5000/redwood
  - Health check: kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=control-plane -o wide
